tier_refine_hint: Reads what you wrote and polishes it. The original stays put; results land in a new section.
tier_organize_hint: Attaches structure and metadata. Always goes through propose → confirm → apply.
tier_gather_hint: Brings things in from outside. The original source is kept intact.
plan_only_badge: Guidance only · not run directly from a menu
list_reads: Restructures the body into a list.
list_detail: Reads the full body of the section you're currently viewing and restructures it into a bullet or checklist, inserted as a new section. The original section stays untouched.
organize_reads: Polishes the body into a cleaner new section.
organize_detail: Reads the full body of the section you're currently viewing, fixes spelling, and restructures paragraphs into a new, more readable section. This is cleanup, not summarization — length isn't cut down much.
summarize_reads: Summarizes the body into a new section.
summarize_detail: Reads the full body of the section you're currently viewing and creates a new section with just the key points. Dates, names, and figures are preserved.
proofread_reads: Fixes only the body's spelling and spacing.
proofread_detail: Reads the full body of the section you're currently viewing and fixes spelling, spacing, and typos only. Content, structure, and tone are left unchanged.
metadata_reads: Reads the body to suggest a title and tags.
metadata_detail: Reads the full body of the current note and suggests a title, tags, year, region, and folder. It's a suggestion only — nothing changes until you confirm it in the review dialog.
diagram_reads: Extracts people and relationships into a diagram.
diagram_detail: Reads the full body of the section you're currently viewing and extracts people, organizations, events, and their relationships into a new diagram section.
diagram_edit_reads: Applies only the requested change to the diagram.
diagram_edit_detail: Reads the diagram source you're viewing and your edit request (not the note's other sections). Applies only the requested change to the existing diagram. Positions and groups you arranged by hand are preserved.
diagram_progress_reads: Reads note text (logs) to update node states.
diagram_progress_detail: Reads the current diagram source and the note body (work logs). Preserves existing diagram structure (nodes/edges/groups) while updating each node's progress state.
diagram_expand_branch_reads: Expands downstream steps from the selected node.
diagram_expand_branch_detail: Reads the current diagram source and the selected reference node. Expands and adds concrete downstream steps and edges originating from that node.
sheet_reads: Builds a new sheet section from the body.
sheet_detail: Reads the full body of the section you're currently viewing and builds a new spreadsheet section — with formulas — from its content.
sheet_edit_reads: Changes only the sheet's requested cells or formulas.
sheet_edit_detail: Reads the current sheet's data and your edit request. Changes only the requested cells, formulas, or charts, keeping the existing row/column layout as-is.
agent_split_reads: Reads the note body and proposes how to split it into multiple notes.
agent_split_detail: Not run from this menu directly. The actual "suggest note split" in the editor's AI menu reads the full body of the current note. Here you can only edit the guidance text it uses. Results are reviewed and applied item-by-item in the plan review screen.
agent_folder_reads: Scans a folder's notes to suggest organizing or merging.
agent_folder_detail: Not run from this menu directly. The real "suggest folder organize/merge" (folder right-click menu) reads only titles, tags, and ids of notes in the folder — never bodies, and never more than 500 notes. Here you can only edit the guidance text it uses. Results are reviewed item-by-item before anything is applied.
agent_workspace_reads: Scans recent notes to suggest a restructure.
agent_workspace_detail: Not run from this menu directly. The real "restructure notebook (AI)" in Settings scans up to 500 of the most recently updated notes (not the whole notebook) in two passes: pass 1 compresses locally (titles/tags only, no bodies) down to at most 30 candidates, and only those 30 are ever sent to the model. Here you can only edit the guidance text it uses.
agent_merge_reads: Finds overlapping notes to suggest a merge.
agent_merge_detail: Not run from this menu directly. Used in three places: reviewing a note-overlap suggestion (Graph tab) from the pet/sidebar chat, and when folder organize or notebook restructure find a merge candidate. In every case, it reads the full bodies of the note(s) involved to draft the merge. Here you can only edit the guidance text that drafting step uses.
ask_note_reads: Reads the open note to answer your question.
ask_note_detail: Reads the sidebar conversation and the content of the note you have open to answer. Answers questions about the note right away in the sidebar/pet assistant chat. Doesn't write or change the note.
find_related_reads: Searches the notebook for notes related to the chat.
find_related_detail: Runs a full-text search (titles and bodies) across the notebook using a query pulled from the conversation, and reads the matching notes' titles and excerpts — not a scan of every note's full body. Shows the results in the sidebar/pet assistant chat.
fill_note_reads: Inserts the chat's draft as a new section in the current note.
fill_note_detail: Reads the sidebar conversation and the full body of the current note to draft the content. Inserts what you asked for as a new section — it never overwrites an existing one. Only works when the sidebar's "allow writing" toggle is on and a note is open.
rename_plan_reads: Scans a folder or the notebook to suggest titles.
rename_plan_detail: Not run from this menu directly. Clicking the preset only sends this text as a chat message — the actual plan is built when you click the reply's "details" chip: if the active note has a folder, that folder is scanned (titles/tags/ids, up to 500 notes, never bodies); otherwise the whole notebook is (up to 500 notes, compressed to at most 30) — that stage follows folder organize's or notebook restructure's own guidance, so editing this text doesn't change the scan results. Sending this guidance through chat does, however, also transmit an excerpt of the open note (all sections joined, up to 4,000 characters) along with the conversation. It only proposes a title change. Nothing is applied until you confirm it in the review screen.
prune_plan_reads: Scans the whole notebook to suggest deletes or merges.
prune_plan_detail: Not run from this menu directly. Clicking the preset only sends this text as a chat message — the actual plan is built when you click the reply's "details" chip, and it always scans the whole notebook, never a single folder (up to 500 notes, compressed to at most 30 by title/tag-overlap signals) — that stage follows notebook restructure's own guidance, so editing this text doesn't change the scan results. Sending this guidance through chat does, however, also transmit an excerpt of the open note (all sections joined, up to 4,000 characters) along with the conversation. Only proposes deletion or merging. Nothing applies until you pick items yourself in the review screen — everything starts unchecked. Deletion is a soft delete (goes to trash).
ai_post_process_reads: Automatically re-suggests a title and tags right after AI writes.
ai_post_process_detail: Re-reads the full body of the note AI just wrote a new section into. Right after AI inserts new content, this runs a metadata (title/tags/etc.) suggestion once more in the background. Still goes through the confirm dialog before anything applies. Turning it off doesn't affect any other AI feature.
link_suggestions_reads: Paste a bare link and it's automatically summarized.
link_suggestions_detail: Fetches the page behind a bare URL you paste into the editor and reads its content. Paste a lone URL and the backend fetches that page and suggests a summary. The target page's content is sent to your AI provider. Off by default.
ai_chat_memory_reads: Automatically detects personal facts in chat and saves them.
ai_chat_memory_detail: Reads the most recent turn of the sidebar conversation (your full message plus the start of the reply). Detects permanent personal facts you mention in conversation (preferences, background, etc.) and saves them to chat memory automatically. You can view and delete saved items in Settings anytime.
collect_nl_source_name: Add a collect source in plain language
collect_nl_source_reads: Type a sentence and it automatically drafts a collect source.
collect_nl_source_detail: Reads the sentence you type to extract a source (RSS/YouTube/etc.). Type something like "subscribe me to this YouTube channel" and it drafts a collect source for you. Managed on the Collect settings page.
ledger_capture_reads: Automatically turns forwarded payment texts into ledger entries.
ledger_capture_detail: Reads payment-notification/SMS text forwarded from your phone via Tasker or Shortcuts to extract line items. Forward a payment notification from your phone (Tasker on Android, Shortcuts on iOS) and AI extracts the item and amount into your ledger. The capture channel itself is opt-in, managed on the Collect settings page.
pet_assistant_reads: Automatically searches for related notes with every chat message.
pet_assistant_detail: Reads the conversation context and, if one is open, the start of the current note. Every message also triggers an automatic notebook search, pulling in excerpts from a few related notes. See the chat-only items above for what each specific action reads. Chat with the pet character or the sidebar to find notes, get explanations, and leave short memos. Turned on/off on the Pet settings page.
